cli.input: --input selects the transaction ledger only; default /app/data/transaction_ledger.json

description: Output contract for the transaction-reporting engine. Shapes, paths, field lists and sort orders only; no derivation rule lives here.

exception_queue.fields_are_exclusive: the listed fields are the whole of the record: it carries these and no others, the same way the output directory carries exactly the three named files
exception_queue.serialisation: one compact JSON object per line, trailing newline

report_lines.fields_are_exclusive: the listed fields are the whole of the record: it carries these and no others, the same way the output directory carries exactly the three named files
report_lines.serialisation: JSON array, two-space indent, trailing newline

field_notes.late_count: counted over every eligible booking at the moment its deadline is worked out, before the confirmation check and before the cap, so a queued booking that was late still counts; it is not the number of report lines carrying late

summary.fields_are_exclusive: the listed fields are the whole of the record: it carries these and no others, the same way the output directory carries exactly the three named files
summary.serialisation: JSON object, two-space indent, trailing newline

policy_fields.deadline_business_days: a non-negative integer no greater than the reporting calendar's horizon_days: the deadline is reached by walking business days forward from the trade day and the calendar describes no day past that horizon, so a larger figure names a deadline the calendar cannot place

transaction_ledger.fields_are_exclusive: the listed fields are the whole of the record: it carries these and no others, the same way the output directory carries exactly the three named files
transaction_ledger.serialisation: JSON array, two-space indent, trailing newline

units.days: integer offsets on the regulatory day grid
units.notional: a non-negative integer in the trade's own currency. Its conversion to usd_notional is exact: notional times the rate table's micro_usd_per_unit divided by a million, floored. The product of those two may exceed what a signed 64-bit integer holds even though every usd_notional the conversion yields sits inside one, so the intermediate cannot be carried in 64 bits
units.usd_notional: whole US dollars; every usd_notional and their reported sum fit a signed 64-bit integer
